title: Compiler error codes and how to fix them
summary: omc refuses a program with omc: line N: error K and exits K; there are no warnings. Drake pins one minimal refusal per code in gate15.sh. I'll show you the ones people hit most: 12 (the 16-register pool, fixed by splitting into helpers and checking the split against a reference), 9 (a word in the wrong place, like new inside a loop), 13 (a name over 8 characters) and 16 (syntax, like an array parameter without its length).
goal: Read omc refusal codes and fix errors 12, 9, 13 and 16 with a verified change.
key_steps: Read the line number and code from omc: line N: error K
Look the code up in the gate15 table
For error 12, split the function into helpers with about 10 live names each
Check the split against a reference and a deliberately wrong variant
For 9, move new to the outermost block; for 13, shorten the name to 8 characters; for 16, fix the syntax (for example state array lengths)

example.code:
note blend.om: refused with error 12. Six parameters, eleven named results and the temporaries of
note the last line all want one of the 16 registers at the same time
fn blend a ulong b ulong c ulong d ulong e ulong f ulong to ulong
ab = mul a b
cd = mul c d
ef = mul e f
ac = add a c
bd = add b d
ce = xor c e
df = xor d f
s1 = add ab cd
s2 = add ef ac
s3 = add bd ce
ret add add add s1 s2 add s3 df add add ab cd ef
end
fn main to int
x = blend 1 2 3 4 5 6
ret int and x 255
end
example.command: Read examples/omega-08-error-codes/POINTER.md. Recorded host output: examples/omega-08-error-codes/output.txt.

common_mistake: Working around error 12 by shortening names or deleting checks. Live values use registers, not long names. Split the function into helpers, keep a reference computation and a negative control that show the split is equivalent.
